To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CrIS fast NH3 physical retrieval is able to retrieve total column amounts and vertical profiles with good accuracy and precision, and is able to capture the vertical distribution of NH3 in the lower troposphere.

the CrIS total column and profile measurements are validated with ground-based Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) instruments in the Network for Detection of Atmospheric Composition and Change (NDACC).
the CrIS fast physics retrieval is a viable product for monitoring NH3 in the troposphere, with a positive total column bias of 1.5% and relative differences within 25-50%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of the fast physical NH3 satellite retrievals with ground-based Fourier transform (FTIR) spectrometers.
the retrieval of atmospheric ammonia from space using the CrIS instrument on the Suomi-NPP satellite.
the validation of the fast physical CrIS NH3 retrieval (FPR), which is based on an optimal estimation approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CrIS fast physical ammonia retrievals are consistent with ground-based FTI R total column observations, but that the CrIS profile retrieval is still under evaluation.
the CrIS CFPR total column and profile measurements are in good agreement with the ground-based FTIR observations.

the CrIS NH3 total column and profile retrievals compare very well with the FTIR observations and the differences are mostly within or near the estimated retrieval uncertainties of both the satellite and ground-based measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CrIS CFPR has good agreement with the FTIR total column and profile measurements.
the CrIS fast NH3 retrievals are generally in agreement with the FTIR data, with the exception that the CrIS retrievals show a slight positive bias at low concentrations.
the CrIS CFPR retrievals are in very good agreement with FTIR observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CrIS fast retrieval algorithm is able to retrieve NH3 total columns and profiles that are in very good agreement with those from ground-based FTIR observations.

the CrIS fast NH3 retrieval can provide useful NH3 measurements, particularly in the middle and upper troposphere, for both the total column and vertical profile, with a good degree of accuracy and precision.
CrIS has good potential to be a useful instrument to study the NH3 atmospheric distribution, especially at higher altitudes where CrIS has better sensitivity.
